chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from al-Wassha' from al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) say: 'If a man marries a woman and sets her dowry at twenty thousand, and gives ten thousand to her father, the dowry is valid, but what he gave to her father is invalid.'

Regarding his statement in the narration: 'If he gives her one dirham from the five hundred dirhams, there is nothing upon her afterwards, nor for her heirs,' this does not mean that once he has stipulated that amount, she has no further claim. It is possible that he intended that if he gives her the one dirham, which is the Sunnah amount for the dowry, and thereby makes her private part permissible to him, she has no further claim afterwards, nor for her heirs. This is what we have explained as valid, and upon this basis, all the narrations are consistent, by the praise and grace of God.
The Sheikh (may God have mercy on him) said: 'And whoever marries a woman and does not specify a dowry for her, and consummates the marriage with her, she is entitled to the dowry of her like.'

key_terms.السُّنَّةُ فِي الْمَهْرِ: The Sunnah amount for the dowry
key_terms.مَهْرُ مِثْلِهَا: Dowry of her like (standard dowry for a woman of similar status)
key_terms.يَسْتَبِيحُ فَرْجَهَا: Makes her private part permissible (consumes the marriage)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a dowry if a husband pays only the sunnah amount instead of a larger stipulated sum, and what happens if no dowry is specified?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the juristic nuance between a fixed stipulated dowry and the sunnah standard, explaining that paying the latter suffices to legitimize conjugal relations, thereby resolving apparent contradictions in hadith literature. This ruling underscores the flexibility in marital contracts, while the final statement establishes 'mahr al-mithl' as the default entitlement when no specific amount is agreed upon, reflecting the principle of equitable compensation in Shia fiqh.
